checkpoints: After each preparation check resolves, distinguish pending from ready before changing completion state.
After a pending result, register exactly one later check for the same preparation lifecycle.
Before applying any asynchronous result or scheduling another retry, verify that the originating lifecycle is still current and mounted.
On ready, stop retrying, clear loading/retry state, and record completion once.
On unmount, cancel any scheduled retry and prevent already-started asynchronous work from publishing state.
forbidden_effects: Do not mark or deliver a file as completed while its preparation status is pending.
Do not create overlapping retry chains from a single pending result.
Do not let an obsolete token or lifecycle result complete the current preparation.
Do not publish state or schedule retries after component unmount.
Do not weaken close/background behavior merely because the dialog is hidden.
lifecycle_identity: A preparation lifecycle is identified by the token captured when its check begins, together with the mounted/current request lifecycle that initiated it.
Retries caused by a pending result belong to the same token lifecycle as the check that produced that result.
A reopen with a next token starts checking that next token; results from an older token must not be attributed to it.
Visibility and preparation lifetime are distinct in the existing public code: close changes visible state but does not cancel an in-flight check.

obligations.text: When a preparation check reports pending, keep checking that same preparation through the supplied retry scheduling boundary.
Record completion—and thereby represent delivery—only after the preparation check reports ready.
A ready result must terminate its retry chain, clear loading and scheduled-retry state, and add the corresponding token to completed no more than once.
A pending result must not add the token to completed; it must arrange one subsequent check after the current check has resolved.
Closing the visible surface must preserve ongoing background preparation behavior already exposed by the public implementations; unmount remains the cancellation boundary.
Asynchronous callbacks and scheduled retries must be scoped to their originating token/lifecycle so that reopening or switching tokens cannot apply an obsolete result to the current preparation.
Preserve the public imperative operations and observable snapshot fields used by DownloadDialog and BackgroundExportPanel.

ordering_barriers: A retry may be scheduled only after the preceding check resolves as pending.
Completion/delivery must occur only after a check for the corresponding token resolves ready.
No further retry may be scheduled after ready has been observed for that lifecycle.
Unmount invalidation must occur before a later promise callback or scheduled callback is allowed to mutate state.
preservation: Preserve start/check behavior that immediately sets loading, increments checkCount, and publishes observable state before invoking the preparation transport.
Preserve close as a visibility change rather than an implicit cancellation of preparation work.
Preserve reopen(nextToken) setting the new token visible and initiating a check.
Preserve snapshot isolation for the completed array.
Preserve BackgroundExportPanel's deduplication of completed tokens and apply equivalent no-duplicate completion semantics where retries are restored.
Preserve the existing data-surface, data-visible, and data-loading render attributes.
scope: Update the public file-preparation polling behavior in src/usePreparation.js used by src/DownloadDialog.jsx.
Keep src/BackgroundExportPanel.jsx behavior consistent where it already models background pending retries, readiness completion, close, and unmount cleanup.
Use the scheduler and cancellation boundaries exposed by src/preparation-api.js; no tests or configuration are in scope.

supporting_evidence.quote: The preparation service can now report that a file is still pending before it becomes ready.
Update the file download dialog so it keeps checking pending preparation and delivers the file only after a ready status.

triggers: Calling start/check begins a preparation check for the token current at that moment.
A pending check result triggers scheduling of the next check.
A ready check result triggers completion/delivery state and ends polling for that lifecycle.
Calling reopen(nextToken) makes the dialog visible and starts checking nextToken.
Component unmount invalidates callbacks and cancels any scheduled retry.
Calling close hides the surface without, by itself, invalidating background preparation.
unknowns: The public sources do not define an actual file-delivery callback or download side effect; the only public completion representation is the completed token list.
The public API does not define a structured status type; existing code treats truthy status as ready and falsy status as pending.
Retry delay, backoff, maximum attempts, timeout, and transport-error policy are not specified.
The task does not state whether multiple explicit start calls may run concurrently or whether they should coalesce.
The task does not specify whether reopening with the same token creates a new lifecycle or resumes an existing one.

No prose requirement defines whether a scheduled retry should continue while the dialog is closed; the public code's close methods only change visibility, so preservation favors continued background work until ready or unmount.
